headline: Every major still sits above its 200-day line while the crowd reads greed, but the day and week are red across the board
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the cleanest signal on the board and it's oddly unanimous: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB are all above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses in place, while DOGE and ADA sit below theirs with no golden cross. That's a majors-versus-the-rest split, not a market-wide trend. Zoom out to the 12-month high and the picture sobers up: BTC is 39.1% off its high, ETH 48.7% off, SOL 60.1% off, XRP 55.2% off. Being above a long-term average after a violent round trip is not the same as being near strength; it just means the average has had time to fall to meet the price.

Momentum is where the story gets interesting. Every asset in the set is negative on MACD (signal line above the MACD line), yet RSI-14 readings cluster in the high 40s to mid-50s: BTC 49.2, ETH 50.9, SOL 51.2, XRP 54.1, BNB 54.4. That's neutral momentum, not oversold, not overbought. So you have a market that just took a real one-day hit (BTC down 2.9%, ETH down 4.3%, SOL down 3.7%, ADA down 4.0%) without momentum indicators confirming panic. Read that as a fast air-pocket move rather than a trend accelerating into a wall. Worth naming plainly: on the day, the week, and the 24-hour tape every asset listed is down, while every one of them is up double digits on the 30-day window (BTC +19.6%, ETH +29.4%, SOL +34.3%, XRP +28.7%). Three different windows, three different stories; none of them cancels the others out.

Positioning adds detail. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0095% per 8 hours (10.4% annualized), a modest cost for holding long perp exposure, paired with a long/short account ratio of 1.72, meaning more accounts are positioned long than short. Liquidations in the past hour were one-sided: $1.74M in long liquidations on BTC and zero on the short side. ETH funding, by contrast, is slightly negative (-0.2% annualized) with an even higher long/short ratio of 1.98, and its hourly liquidations skewed toward longs too ($228K vs $647K, actually short-heavy in dollar terms there). SOL funding is negative at -6.2% annualized despite a long/short ratio of 2.16, an odd mix worth flagging: more long accounts, but the market is paying shorts to hold, which usually shows up when large directional bets sit on the short side even if smaller accounts lean long. Open interest is largest in BTC ($2.2B) and ETH ($1.53B), so this isn't a thin, easily-ignored derivatives book, it's real size responding to a fast move.

Flows are the tension point of the day. BTC spot ETFs posted an inflow of $159.9M on 14 Sep 2026, but the five-session net is an outflow of $302.8M, and same_direction_days of 1 confirms that single day was the outlier, not the trend. ETH ETFs tell the opposite story: inflow of $121.1M on the same day, and the five-session net agrees at +$318.0M. Meanwhile whale wallets moved a net $174.2M onto exchanges over the last 24 hours, led by $76.9M of BTC into Binance and roughly $126M of ETH into Coinbase Institutional. Looking at the weekly whale series, every one of the last four weeks (ending Aug 25 through Sep 15) shows net movement onto exchanges, ranging from $25M to $1.08B. Coins moving toward exchanges is usually read as supply positioning for potential selling, and it's happening in the same week ETH's ETF flows are net positive, which is the kind of contradiction the tape doesn't resolve for you.

Sentiment sits at 69, labeled Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 31 to 74. That's a crowd feeling good on a day when every major asset is red and whales are net moving coins onto exchanges. The gauge and the tape are not agreeing today, and that gap is itself the most useful thing on the board. Stablecoin float is up a modest 1.36% over 30 days to $310.3B, dry powder that's growing slowly rather than surging. Worth watching from here: whether BTC's five-session ETF outflow reverses or deepens, whether the whale-to-exchange trend that's held for four straight weeks breaks, and whether MACD crosses back above signal on any major as a sign momentum is turning rather than just resting.
